formula: docvis ~ outwork + female + age + factor(edlevel) + (1 | id)
notes: Read rwm5yr.Rd: German health registry panel 1984 to 1988 (Hilbe and Greene 2008), id the patient id and year the wave. The help example fits pooled glm(docvis ~ outwork + female + age + factor(edlevel), family=poisson) and, in dontrun, nbinomial and glm.nb; the Modeling Count Data code the package ships (inst/HILBE_SCRIPTS/HILBE-MCD-Rcode.r) uses only its 1984 wave (rwm1984 <- subset(rwm5yr, year==1984)) in GLMs. A panel fitted only pooled, so id is rendered as a random intercept (panel ruling). hospvis is the alternate response; edlevel1 to edlevel4 are the dummies of edlevel. year, married, kids, hhninc, educ and self are usable columns. formula: accident ~ op + co.70.74 + co.75.79 + offset(log(service)) + (1 | ship), gamma-distributed multiplicative ship effect by ship
notes: Read ships.Rd (McCullagh and Nelder 1989; Hardin and Hilbe): accidents per ship, construction and operation period, log(service) the offset; the page says ship can be used as a panel identifier. The help fits glm and glm.nb and, in dontrun, gee(accident ~ op + co.70.74 + co.75.79 + offset(log(service)), family=poisson, corstr=exchangeable, id=ship), so the cluster is rendered as a random intercept; GEE is no mixed model. Stata's xtpoisson manual fits the same data with a ship random effect (stata_ships, in the registry). co.65.69 is a dummy the example leaves out; a ship-period never operated has no accident and no service. Hand check #162: yes by the outside check: Hilbe (Negative Binomial Regression, 2nd ed., 2011, chapter 14, p. 481) fits this formula by xtpoisson accident op co_70_74 co_75_79, exposure(service) i(ship) re, whose gamma-distributed multiplicative ship effect the formula names, as for wooldridge airfare (the page was not seen here, the book being paywalled). The six ship-periods never operated miss service and accident, so 34 of 40 rows enter. The Stata manual's gamma and normal fits with co_65_69 (stata_ships) and Hilbe's random-effects negative binomial (p. 485) share this response and grouping and file no row. The table equals stata_ships ships.dta in every cell, its columns renamed.

formula: y ~ crack0 + (1 | specimen); rand.family = inverse.Gamma(log); resid.model = ~ cycle + (1 | specimen)
notes: crack has no help page (spaMM-internal.Rd: not documented but used in an example). The example in phi-resid.model.Rd, citing Lee, Nelder and Pawitan (2006) chapter 11: HLfit(y~crack0+(1|specimen), family=Gamma(log), data=crack, rand.family=inverse.Gamma(log), resid.model=list(formula=~cycle+(1|specimen))), a double HGLM; tests/testthat/test-dhglm.R fits the same with HLmethod=REML. RULE GAP: the specimen effect of the mean is inverse-gamma on the log scale, not Gaussian, and a second specimen effect enters the dispersion model; both are named in the formula. cycle enters only the dispersion model. The columns are undocumented. Hand check #162: stands by its ruling (a location-scale model is named in the formula); 21 specimens of 9 to 12 cycles. test-dhglm.R's variant with a cycle slope in the dispersion's specimen effect, its correlation fixed at -0.5, shares this response and grouping and files no row.

Read the ohio help page (LeSage and Pace 2009 web data; col 23 the median of 4th grade prof scores, col 5 the district irn) and Alam, Ronnegard and Shen (2015, R Journal 7(2), section Ohio elementary school grades data set): We regress the median of 4th grade proficiency scores, y, on an intercept, based on school districts, y_ij = mu + v_j + e_ij with v CAR-distributed over adjacent districts, fitted as hglm(y = ohioMedian$MedianScore, X = X, Z = model.matrix(~ 0 + district), rand.family = CAR(D = ohioDistrictDistMat)); hglm.Rd fits the same as hglm(fixed = MedianScore ~ 1, random = ~ 1 | district, rand.family = CAR(D = ohioDistrictDistMat), data = ohioMedian). RULE GAP: the model is documented on ohioMedian, the derived subset of this table (MedianScore is V23 and district is V5 without its last digit, as the first rows show) for the 1,860 schools the paper matched to a census district; filed on this superset, ohioMedian excluded as derived. V1 (zip), V2 and V3 (zip centroid coordinates), V4 and V21 (building ids) are ids or coordinates; V22 and V26 to V30 are alternate responses. Hand check #162: stands by its ruling (a subset fit stays on the whole object). The paper's district is floor(V5 / 10), which relabels V5's 599 levels one to one to the names of ohioDistrictDistMat, so V5 stays the grouping factor; the 1,860 schools of ohioMedian lie in 562 of the matrix's 616 districts, all 616 kept as levels.
